A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VoxEval research work. Their main text, tables, figures, equations and appendices are readable and can be matched across the additions and renumbering.

before.justification: Tables 5–8 report original evaluations of five spoken language models, including accuracy across audio conditions, modality combinations and mathematical reasoning settings.

after.justification: v4 retains original model evaluations and adds answer-extraction validation, cascaded/API model comparisons, prompting experiments and statistical analyses in Appendices A–D.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, GPT-4o verbalization, speech synthesis, audio perturbations and Whisper-plus-string-matching scoring procedure remain unchanged. Added comparisons, validation studies and implementation disclosures do not establish a change to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain 13,938 MMLU-derived SpeechQA pairs across 56 subjects and the same speaker, speaking-style and acoustic coverage. The added studies use retained subjects or audit the scoring pipeline; subset selection and different prompting configurations do not expand task coverage.

E2.justification: v4 retains the five original SLMs and adds Whisper + Llama-3.1-8B to Table 5. Appendix B/Table 10 compares GLM-4-Voice with Whisper-large-v3 cascades using Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen2-7B-Instruct, plus gpt-4o-audio-preview. This substantially broadens comparisons to cascaded and closed-source systems.

E3.justification: New protocols include manual validation of 30 responses to ten randomly selected questions using WER/CER and answer-extraction accuracy; a comparison using 12 subjects and their first 100 questions each; and GLM-4-Voice studies varying non-CoT examples from zero to five and CoT examples from zero to three. The original main evaluation protocol remains.

E4.justification: Appendix A adds scoring-pipeline validation and examination of an extraction failure. Appendix C adds controlled shot-count sensitivity analysis with and without CoT, while Appendix D tests audio-condition effects statistically. These substantially extend the retained modality, truncation, box-plot and response-case analyses.

E5.justification: v4 adds Friedman tests across 11 audio conditions using 56 subject accuracies, followed by pairwise Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Bonferroni correction. Table 12 and Figure 3 report significance results absent from v3. Both versions still state that each experiment was performed once; additional repeated runs are not reported.

E6.justification: Table 8 substantially revises CoT results for SPIRIT-LM, Moshi and GLM-4-Voice. For example, GLM-4-Voice's high-school-math CoT/Cut string-matching accuracy changes from 14.44% to 5.19%, without a corresponding stated protocol revision. v4 also adds cascade/API scores, 29/30 correct answer extractions, shot-count results and statistical findings. The original overall scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix D adds an explicit mathematical calculation of 55 pairwise comparisons from 11 conditions and the Bonferroni cutoff of 0.05/55 = 0.000909 in Equations 1–2. This is a limited formal addition supporting the statistical analysis; Algorithm 1 remains unchanged and no theoretical propositions or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The introduction changes from describing support for end-to-end speech evaluation to explicitly claiming, with a knowledge qualifier, that VoxEval is the first benchmark supporting it. This sharpens the novelty claim alongside VoiceBench's reclassification. The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion otherwise retain their substantive claims.

C2.justification: v4 qualifies the reasoning interpretation and adds explanations of elementary-math CoT benefits, possible guessing, and a trade-off between reasoning and answer formatting. It also interprets cascaded/API performance gaps and scoring reliability. Section 6 replaces the single-model modality-evaluation limitation with limitations of synthetic speech, materially changing the stated applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v4 specifies the MMLU test set, adds noise SNR settings in Table 13, and clarifies direct-answer prompting and Alloy case selection. These are disclosures rather than established changes to existing experiments. It removes v3 Appendix B's single NVIDIA RTX A6000 hardware statement. Dataset access information and conversion prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 and Table 2 reclassify VoiceBench from supporting end-to-end evaluation to evaluating textual output only. New citations to MinMo and VITA-Audio motivate speech-to-speech evaluation through reported modality-performance gaps. The remainder of the related-work coverage is largely retained.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized rewrites to the introduction, robustness explanation, reasoning discussion and limitations, corrects terminology, and adds correspondence and funding information. Four analytical appendices precede the retained appendices. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 expands Table 5 from one column to full width with an additional comparator, adds five tables covering validation, comparisons, prompting, statistics and noise settings, and introduces a four-panel significance heatmap. Existing Figures 1–2 are unchanged; the earlier appendix tables and prompt figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The added comparator controls, scoring audit and statistical tests strengthen the context and evidential support for v3's findings. The gain is limited by the 30-response audit and overstatements in the new analysis: Appendix C claims consistent one-shot CoT improvement, although Table 11 shows high-school accuracy falling from 0.06 to 0.04. Removing hardware information and the still-applicable single-model modality limitation also weakens reporting.
